description: The Global Findex Database of the World Bank is a demand-side survey of how adults around the world access and use financial services, running since 2011. It covers account ownership, digital payments, saving, borrowing, financial health and the gender gap, and the 2025 edition adds a Digital Connectivity Tracker on access to and use of mobile technology; it reports, for example, that 40 per cent of adults in developing economies saved in a financial account in 2024, that 56 per cent could reliably access extra money in an emergency, and that one in four adults in low- and middle-income economies faced a natural disaster in the past three years. The site offers the report, interactive visualisations, a figure builder and downloadable datasets, with an archive of earlier waves and a methodology page; access is free. The Gates Foundation and Mastercard Foundation support it. The licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: data are national survey estimates every few years, not administrative records, and small subgroups have large sampling error. For simulation it gives the share of people who depend on accounts, mobile money or cash, and their coping capacity after shocks, for social vulnerability and financial access analyses. Related catalogue records include the World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey and the BIS CPMI Red Book statistics.
